dedupe_keys.name: economic value of health benefits of a proposed downtown park peterborough canada

description: This study applied an ecohealth economic valuation framework to estimate the economic value of health benefits from developing a proposed park in the downtown core of Peterborough, Ontario. The authors note that park use is linked to better physical and mental health and that more green space can reduce harm from air pollutants, heat, noise and climate-related health risks, yet few studies put a money value on these benefits. Coverage: one proposed small urban park. Access: open-access article in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (2023). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: an ex-ante appraisal of a proposal, relying on transferred dose-response and cost values. Outcome: annual benefits of about CAD 133,000, including CAD 109,877 in avoided economic burden of physical inactivity. Simulation uses: valuing health co-benefits of park and cooling-space investments in capital planning. Related records: the Getxo green space benefit-cost analysis and the TPL ParkServe layer.
